lines: Every manufacturer knows its direct suppliers.
The dangerous surprises sit deeper:
one missing input, three tiers away, can stop the finished product.
Markov makes that exposure visible.
Start with the supplier records: parts, compliance, locations, and dependencies.
Single-source suppliers are marked because a disruption there leaves no recorded alternative.
The architecture is designed to keep this sensitive information local.
A rare-earth export licence is suspended in Chile.
Altiplano is hit directly: single-source and already non-compliant.
One tier down, two suppliers.
Two tiers down, two more.
Three tiers down, the finished powertrain module.
The code traces the dependency chain.
The monitor checks new disruptions without waiting to be asked.
It records routine events and flags those needing attention.
Here’s a replay of its local check.
Detected. Flagged for approval.
The output is a risk summary and an email draft for a person to approve.
Response delivery is not connected in this preview.
If the model is unavailable, deterministic analysis still works,
and templates supply the wording.
Knowing the cause is only the start.
Combine stock, schedules, orders, and quality records.
Protect the priority order, then switch to independent kits.
The shortage remains, but production keeps moving.
Review the plan and reassess as conditions change.
